# Competitive Comparison

PatternFly 6 vs. MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI, and Radix UI + Tailwind CSS.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## npm Weekly Downloads (March 26 – April 1, 2026)

| Library | Package | Weekly Downloads |
|---------|---------|-----------------|
| Radix UI | @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu | 36,212,245 [27] |
| MUI | @mui/material | 8,492,554 [24] |
| Ant Design | antd | 3,021,044 [25] |
| Chakra UI | @chakra-ui/react | 1,258,551 [26] |
| PatternFly | @patternfly/react-core | 135,213 [23] |

Radix downloads are inflated by shadcn/ui, which depends on Radix primitives
as transitive dependencies [27]. PatternFly downloads are ~63x smaller than MUI.

Radix has the broadest support (React 16.8+). PatternFly, MUI match (React 17+).

## Component Count

| Library | Count | Source |

| Radix UI | 13+ core primitives | [35] |

PatternFly's 92 components include enterprise-specific components (Login Page,
Masthead, Notification Drawer) not commonly found in general-purpose libraries.
Chakra UI v2 count (53) may differ from current v3.34.0 [40]. Radix provides
headless primitives only, supplemented by consumer UIs like shadcn/ui [35].

## Bundle Size (Bundlephobia, April 2, 2026)

| Library | Minified | Gzipped |
|---------|----------|---------|
| MUI 7.3.9 | 514 KB | 146 KB [37] |
| PatternFly 6.4.1 (JS) | 550 KB | 151 KB [36] |
| PatternFly 6.4.1 (CSS) | 2.17 MB | 131 KB [36] |
| Chakra UI 3.34.0 | 1.0 MB | 270 KB [39] |
| Ant Design 6.3.5 | 1.4 MB | anomalous (est.) [38] |

PatternFly's JS bundle (550 KB / 151 KB gzip) is comparable to MUI (514 KB /
146 KB gzip), but PatternFly additionally ships 2.17 MB of CSS (131 KB gzip) [36].
Ant Design's reported gzip of 6.2 KB is anomalous and likely a Bundlephobia
measurement error [38]. All libraries support tree-shaking via ESM.

A third-party Cockpit starter-kit migration showed PatternFly React compressed
JS at 80 kB vs. PatternFly Elements (Lit) at 29 kB, with the 23 kB CSS file
eliminated entirely [34].

## Accessibility Claims

| Library | Claim | Details |
|---------|-------|---------|
| PatternFly | WCAG 2.2 Level AA | aXe automated, VoiceOver/NVDA/JAWS manual, 12 specific WCAG criteria listed [5] |
| Radix UI | WAI-ARIA compliant | Keyboard nav, screen reader tested, focus management, RTL [35] |
| MUI | Not verified | — |
| Ant Design | Not verified | — |
| Chakra UI | Not verified | Skip Nav + Visually Hidden components suggest focus [40] |

PatternFly makes the most specific, auditable accessibility claims with named
WCAG criteria. Caveat: PatternFly.org website scorecard (November 2024) showed
133 unresolved violations [10].

## Design Philosophy

| Library | Philosophy |
|---------|-----------|
| PatternFly | Enterprise design system: consistency, reduce redundancy, unified language [11] |
| Radix UI | Unstyled headless primitives: composable, incremental adoption [35] |
| MUI | Material Design implementation (common knowledge, not verified from fetched data) |
| Ant Design | Enterprise-class design language, CSS-in-JS with @layer directives |
| Chakra UI | Composable, style props + theme (common knowledge, not verified from fetched data) |

## Styling Approach

| Library | Approach |
|---------|----------|
| PatternFly | CSS custom properties (design tokens), 3-layer hierarchy, class-based theming [1][6] |
| Radix UI | Unstyled — consumer provides all styles, commonly paired with Tailwind [35] |
| MUI | Emotion/styled-components, sx prop (not verified from fetched data) |
| Ant Design | CSS-in-JS with CSS custom properties, @layer antd directives |
| Chakra UI | Style props + @emotion/react (peer dep) [21] |

## Gaps and Limitations

- MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI component counts not verified from fetched sources
- MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI accessibility claims not verified
- Bundle size comparison does not account for tree-shaking in real applications
- Download counts are a single-week snapshot; no historical trend data
- Ant Design gzip figure from Bundlephobia appears anomalous [38]
- TypeScript support quality, SSR/RSC compatibility, and release cadence not compared across competitors
